shifts.summary: The shift was overall easy to moderate, with candidates reporting about 20–21 well‑attempted questions. Reasoning was generally easy, featuring lengthy and analytical items, while quantitative was moderate to difficult with many advanced problems and time pressure. General Ability showed mixed difficulty, from easy current‑affairs to difficult constitutional topics. English was mostly easy, though a few found it a bit tough. Technical glitches caused extra waiting time and a delayed start.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Testbook noted some lengthy reasoning questions and two arithmetic items; Madhuvan mentioned more analytical questions, about eight; timing was tight for reasoning.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: Testbook said GA was easy with a few current‑affairs items; Madhuvan found it difficult with only 1–2 current‑affairs questions; SSC covered many topics such as language, history, dance, security dialogue, and constitutional articles.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Testbook said many advanced, out‑of‑the‑box questions with high time pressure; Madhuvan reported 25 questions in 15 minutes and harder than earlier; SSC included varied topics like clock angle and jet‑stream altitude.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Testbook found English generally easy though one candidate felt it a bit tough; Madhuvan described it as moderate with paragraph and PQRS type questions; SSC covered vocabulary such as antonyms, synonyms and meanings.

asked.q: Lengthy reasoning question that required more time.
Arithmetic question from the reasoning set.

What is the main purpose of the Quad security dialogue?
If a clock’s minute hand moves π/6 rad from 12:00, at which minute mark does it point?
How many frames are there in a standard ten‑pin bowling game?
Which address is same or different?

observations: Overall exam was perceived as easy to moderate, with many candidates finding reasoning and English easy.
Quantitative section was noted as moderate to difficult with many advanced questions and high time pressure.
General Ability showed mixed difficulty, ranging from easy current‑affairs to difficult constitutional topics.
Technical issues caused extra wait time and delayed start for some candidates.
disagreements: One report called GA easy, another called it difficult (reports differ).
One report said Quant moderate, another said moderate to difficult (reports differ).
